summary: Peer Q2 implemented. Paired cross-play with 500 shared seeds per condition shows informed Mafia seats gaining 8.6 points while informed Village seats gain 0.2 to 0.8 points, i.e. nothing. A new vote-coordination diagnostic attributes the Mafia gain to deterministic bloc voting rather than inference, so your lift condition is NOT satisfied and peer step 6 applies.
round_goal: Implement fixed-baseline paired cross-play with shared seeds and identical role schedules, make terminal cross-play faction win rate the primary outcome, and apply the peer's lift condition.

design_delivered.baseline: plain = uniform random legal target, frozen, cannot learn
design_delivered.seeding: seeds 0-499 identical across all seven conditions
design_delivered.role_schedule_check: the artifact verifies from the recorded episodes that every condition played the same Mafia assignment for every seed, rather than asserting it
design_delivered.arm_assignment: arms are assigned by role, read from the seed's schedule at setup time; this is experiment design and never reaches a policy, which still consumes only its own ActorView. The existing runtime guard, decision-path AST audit and per-episode empirical check all still pass.

primary_outcome.significance_note: At 500 episodes the standard error on a proportion near 0.15 is about 0.016, so the village deltas are inside noise and the mafia delta is about five standard errors.

mechanism_diagnostic.why_it_exists: To distinguish inference from coordination before claiming either. The environment eliminates the plurality target, so a coordinated pair can choose the elimination without out-reasoning anyone.
mechanism_diagnostic.finding: Informed Mafia seats vote unanimously at rate 1.000 against a 0.181 chance baseline, because both seats run identical code on identical private knowledge, and that shared target is then the plurality 96.3% of the time. The four village seats scatter across about 2.6 distinct targets, so two coordinated votes usually top the tally.

gate_verdict.reasoning: Your lift condition requires a reproducible gain attributable to belief or planning rather than tie-breaking or channel artifacts. A reproducible gain exists, but the mechanism diagnostic attributes it to deterministic bloc voting. And the capability the gate exists to validate is hidden-information inference, which is the village side's task: informed village seats gain 0.2 to 0.8 points, which is no effect.
gate_verdict.peer_step_6: Applied. Since corrected belief and belief_planning still fail against a fixed baseline on the village side, no further SecretMafia rule tuning is planned and the substrate or feature model is treated as insufficient for the intended high-skill claim.
what_is_established: harness, seeding, schedule verification, information boundary and metric demotion are in place and tested
the native channel works and the belief discriminates where evidence exists
a cross-play effect exists and is fully attributed by a diagnostic instead of asserted
zero information leakage in every condition
what_is_not_established: that the village can use belief or planning to find Mafia better than random
that the mafia gain survives an opponent that also coordinates or models the bloc

methodological_gap_i_am_flagging_rather_.issue: The frozen baseline is uniform random. It cannot coordinate, so it is maximally exploitable by bloc voting, and part of the +8.6 point mafia delta measures the baseline's incoherence rather than SCK's strength.
methodological_gap_i_am_flagging_rather_.what_i_did_not_do: I did not add a coordination heuristic to SCK or tune the evidence model to make the number look better. Per your Q4 reasoning, replacing one author bias with another is the failure mode to avoid.
methodological_gap_i_am_flagging_rather_.what_i_recommend: Strengthen the fixed baseline set, for example with a coordination-capable fixed heuristic, before any positive strength claim in either direction.

decision_requested.question: Which of the following should round 8 be?
options: A. Your Q4 path: build the symmetric evidence feature set and replay-calibrate it on a training seed partition, freeze it, and evaluate on held-out seeds, requiring the gain on the village side.
B. Add village-side vote coordination as a first-class capability, since the diagnostic shows the informed village scatters instead of concentrating on its best suspect.
C. Strengthen the baseline set first, so a coordination effect cannot masquerade as cognition, and re-run cross-play before changing SCK at all.
D. Your Q6 path now: move to a mixed-motive peaceful repeated game, since the target StoryBox use is coordination under mixed interests and SecretMafia structurally punishes the side that must infer.
E. Something else, or stop the SCK line and return to StoryBox work with the recorded negative result.
decision_requested.my_recommendation: C then A, with D as the strategic redirect. C is cheap and removes the largest threat to the validity of every number so far, A is the capability you actually want validated, and the mechanism finding makes me doubt that SecretMafia is the right place to validate a capability whose real use is peaceful mixed-interest coordination.
decision_requested.what_would_change_my_mind: If a coordination-capable baseline still loses to informed Mafia by a similar margin, the bloc effect is robust and the mafia result becomes real evidence about the planner rather than about baseline weakness.

limits: Self-play and cross-play are both all-local-policy games; no external model or human opponent is involved.
6 players, discussion_rounds=3, deterministic template discussion, so persuasion_delta remains unavailable.
The evidence model is still the hand-specified one; the replay-calibrated model is not implemented.
The mafia gain is measured against a baseline that cannot coordinate, as flagged above.
action_required: Please choose A to E for round 8, with a reason. I am stopping at the gate rather than picking for you, because your step 6 explicitly forbids continuing to tune SecretMafia rules after this result and the remaining options differ in kind rather than in degree.
